recipes.description: The sauce behind every Sunday dinner: low, slow, and worth the wait. This entry shows the format each family recipe will follow.

handwritingNotes.note: The card reads '2 or 3 cloves' and the number is hard to make out. We went with 3. If you remember it differently, tell Joe or Jim.

ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
A handful of fresh basil leaves, torn
recipes.sourceNote: Example entry transcribed from a handwritten recipe card, October 2026. Wording preserved as written.
steps: Warm the olive oil in a large, heavy pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook, stirring, until soft and golden at the edges, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and tomato paste and cook 1 minute more, until fragrant.
Pour in the wine, if using, and scrape up anything stuck to the bottom of the pot.
Add the crushed tomatoes, oregano, and sugar. Stir well.
Bring to a gentle simmer, then lower the heat and cook uncovered for about 3 hours, stirring every 20 minutes or so, until thick and deep red.
Season with salt and pepper, stir in the basil, and serve.
recipes.title: Sunday Tomato Sauce
